title_he: הסכם קיבוצי (מסגרת) — הקצאת מסגרת עלות התוספות ותוספת 2011
title_en: Collective (Framework) Agreement — Allocation of the Supplements Cost Envelope and the 2011 Supplement
summary_en: Fixes the public-sector wage-cost envelope for 1.1.2009-30.6.2012 at 1.7857% for each of 2009, 2010 and 2011 plus 0.8929% for January-June 2012, and sets the dates on which it is released: 2.25% from 1.1.2011, a top-up to 4.25% from 1.1.2012 and a top-up to 6.25% from 1.1.2013, all computed on a base of the monthly average of combined salary, seniority supplement and cost-of-living supplements over January-December 2010. It creates 'Tosefet 2011', a new 2.25% percentage supplement paid at a uniform rate to every employee in every rank, which counts as salary for hourly value, severance pay, pension, study fund and the pensionable determining salary, and it orders the calculation Tosefet 2001 before Tosefet 2009 before Tosefet 2011. It introduces a childcare supplement (tosefet me'onot) of NIS 300 a month for a first child and NIS 200 for a second, payable from 1.9.2011 to a mother of a child under 5 and index-linked annually from January 2012, and raises employer and employee pension contributions by 0.5% from 1.1.2011 and a further 0.5% from 1.1.2013. It is signed with the General Histadrut and does not itself cover the teachers' ranking; it reaches teachers only through the separate implementation agreements negotiated under section 155(a) of the Ofek Hadash base agreement.

title_he: הסכם קיבוצי (מסגרת)
title_en: Collective (Framework) Agreement [public sector, 2016]
summary_en: Fixes the public-sector wage-cost envelope for 1.1.2013-31.12.2017 at 7.5% — 1.5% for each of the five years 2013 to 2017 — and releases it in five tranches: 1% from 1.7.2016, top-up to 2.75% from 1.3.2017, to 4.25% from 1.1.2018, to 6% from 1.6.2018 and to 7.5% from 1.12.2018, on a base of the monthly average of pay components over January-December 2015. The first tranche is paid as 'Tosefet Sheklit 2016', a flat shekel supplement whose amount is solved from A + B = C so that its total cost equals 1% of the base for each calculation group, pro-rated for part-time and index-linked each January from 2017; where no distributing agreement is signed by the stated dates, default allocations create 'Tosefet Ahuzit 2016' at 1.375% from 1.3.2017, rising to 2.125% from 1.1.2018, 3% from 1.6.2018 and 3.75% from 1.12.2018, with the residue going to enlarge the shekel supplement. It also pays a one-time grant of NIS 2,000 in two equal parts of NIS 1,000, updates 'special supplements' and index-linked supplements on the same 1%/2.75%/4.25%/6%/7.5% ladder, grants working parents a one-hour shortening of each of the last ten working days of August (ten hours in all) or one leave day instead, and increases the pensionable determining salary of employees who retired between 1.1.2013 and 30.11.2018 by Y = X*A + X*B*C. The envelope is cut to 7.425% for uniform-ranking and MAHAR employees in local authorities and to 7.29% for social workers. It is signed with the General Histadrut; the teachers' ranking is not in the Annex A list of covered rankings.

title_he: הסכם קיבוצי (מסגרת) — המגזר הציבורי 2023
title_en: Collective (Framework) Agreement — Public Sector 2023
summary_en: Runs to 31.12.2027 and sets the public-sector pay increases directly rather than as a cost envelope. It pays a one-time grant of up to NIS 6,000 computed as S = C * B * A, where A is 6,000, B is the number of months worked in the calculation period 1.10.2020-31.3.2023 divided by 30 and C is the average post fraction; it creates 'Tosefet Sheklit 2023' of NIS 400 a month for a full-time employee from 1.7.2023, raised by NIS 100 to NIS 500 from 1.10.2024, pro-rated for part-time and counting as salary for hourly value, severance, pension and study fund; and it creates 'Tosefet Ahuzit 2024' of 2% from 1.12.2024, raised by 1.5 points to 3.5% from 1.4.2025, by 1.5 points to 5% from 1.4.2026 and by 1 point to 6% from 1.4.2027 (the last step being a default if no distributing agreement is signed by 31.1.2027 for the 1% reserved by § 50). Hourly-paid staff get NIS 2.2 per hour from 1.7.2023 plus NIS 0.58 from 1.10.2024, and daily-paid staff NIS 19.2 (five-day week) or NIS 16 (six-day week) per day from 1.7.2023, rising to NIS 24 and NIS 20 from 1.10.2024. It shortens the working week without loss of pay from 42 to 41 hours (177.667 hours a month) from 1.10.2023 and to 40 hours (173.333 hours a month) from 1.9.2024. Chapter (יא) governs employees paid on the teachers' scale by linkage: they receive the 2023 and 2024 supplements but any increase paid to them for 1.1.2020 onwards by virtue of the linkage to teachers' pay is set off against them, up to the full amount of the two supplements.

title_he: הסכם קיבוצי לתחילת יישום הרפורמה במערכת החינוך
title_en: Collective Agreement for the Commencement of the Education-System Reform
summary_en: A temporary agreement, in force from 1.9.2007 to 15.12.2007, that starts the six-year Ofek Hadash reform in state primary schools and junior high schools while the full agreement is negotiated; the reform is to be phased in from 1.9.2007 and completed no later than 1.9.2012, school by school on the Ministry of Education's list, and every new teacher is employed on reform terms from day one. It rewrites the working week for a 100% post: 36 hours a week in a primary school, of which 26 are frontal class hours, 5 are individual or small-group hours (up to 5 pupils) and 5 are 'stay' hours; and 36 hours in a junior high school, of which 23 are frontal, 4 individual and 9 stay. A 'mother teacher' — at least a 79% post and a mother of a child under 14 — may cut half an hour a day, 2.5 weekly stay hours, without any reduction in salary or post fraction; a teacher below a 50% post may not move onto reform terms without the approval of the Ministry's teaching-personnel division. A substitution hour is paid at 125% of the hourly value, and a teacher who does a substitution hour in place of a stay hour and takes that stay hour on another day is paid both the 125% and the ordinary 100%.

title_he: הסכם קיבוצי ליישום רפורמת "אופק חדש" במערכת החינוך
title_en: Collective Agreement for the Implementation of the "Ofek Hadash" (New Horizon) Reform in the Education System
summary_en: The founding instrument of Ofek Hadash pay: 160 sections, in force from 1.9.2008 until the reform is completed on 1.9.2013, covering every teaching-ranking employee in state kindergartens, primary schools and junior high schools including special education. It fixes the working week (36 hours for a full post: 26 frontal + 5 individual + 5 stay in a primary school, 23 + 4 + 9 in a junior high, with reduced frontal loads for grade heads), new nine-rank combined-salary tables for BA and MA holders updated to 1.12.2008 and topped up to 3% from 1.12.2009 and thereafter at cost-of-living dates, and the rules for placing and promoting teachers on them: two years in rank 1 and in rank 2, three years in each of ranks 3, 4 and 5, and three years in each of ranks 6, 7 and 8, with ranks 7, 8 and 9 capped at 10%, 5% and 3% of all teaching posts and a maximum wait of 3, 4 and 5 years once the conditions are met. It lists the role supplements that survive the reform — homeroom teacher 10% of combined salary, first-grade homeroom 11.5%, special-education teacher 5.5%, 8.5%, 9% or 14%, inclusion teacher 5.5% or 9%, subject coordinator 6% (primary) or 8% (junior high), road-safety, security and lab coordinators 6%, 6% and 3%, social-education coordinator 6% or 10%, grade head 6% or 7%, assessment coordinator 6% — capping a teacher at two of them, adds 5% for a doctorate and 14% for teaching a gifted class, and pays substitution hours and school activities at 125% of hourly value, school activities being capped at 18 hours per half school year. Hourly value is combined salary divided by 4.33 weeks times 36 hours; employment is capped at a 100% post in no more than two schools with a 42-hour ceiling; attendance is clocked, counted from no earlier than 7:45 (7:00 for principals and first deputies). Section 155(a) binds the parties to negotiate the application to teachers of any general public-sector framework agreement, defaulting to a uniform increase of the salary tables for reform teachers and a separate line-item supplement for the rest.

title_he: הסכם קיבוצי ליישום רפורמת "אופק חדש" במערכת החינוך
title_en: Collective Agreement for the Implementation of the "Ofek Hadash" (New Horizon) Reform in the Education System
summary_en: The signed, stamped copy of the full Ofek Hadash agreement of 25.12.2008, carrying the recitals, the signature blocks and three 'reform annex' working-week tables that the unstamped copy does not have. The annexes tabulate, for every post fraction from 100% down to about 33%, the split of the week into frontal, individual and stay hours for primary-school teachers and for junior-high teachers, in three age bands (under 50, from 50, and from 55 — the last not applying to new teachers from school year 5768), together with the stay-hour reduction for a mother teacher. In a primary school a 100% post is 26 frontal + 5 individual + 5 stay = 36 hours, falling to 24 frontal (34 hours) from age 50 and 23 frontal with 4 individual (32 hours) from age 55; in a junior high a 100% post is 23 frontal + 4 individual + 9 stay = 36 hours, falling to 21 frontal (34 hours) from age 50 and 20 frontal with 3 individual (32 hours) from age 55. The mother-teacher stay reduction is 2.5 hours in a primary school and 6.5 hours in a junior high at a full post, and is available only where her total post across all schools is 79% or more.

title_he: החלטת ועדת מעקב — קידום בדרגות של עובדי הוראה
title_en: Monitoring Committee Decision — Rank Promotion of Teaching Staff
summary_en: A decision of the Supreme Monitoring Committee under section 160 of the Ofek Hadash agreement of 25.12.2008, registered as a collective agreement on 9.9.2015. It rescues the rank promotion of a teacher on reform terms whose employment in the state service ends on 31 August and whose required stay period in the previous rank would only end on that same day: if all the other promotion conditions were met on the 31 July before, the teacher is promoted as though the stay period had ended on 31 July, and the promotion takes effect from 1 August preceding the end of employment — so the higher rank is paid for the final month rather than lost. It also provides that teachers who first came onto reform terms in November 2007, but who taught in the state service in September and October 2007, are treated for stay-period purposes as having started on 1.9.2007, and that they too get the benefit of the rule above.

summary_en: Applies to teachers, under section 155(a) of the Ofek Hadash agreement, the first tranche of the cost envelope set by section 5.1.1 of the public-sector framework agreement of 12.1.2011 — 2.25% from 1.1.2011. title_he: הסכם קיבוצי — השלמה ותיקון של ההסכמות אליהן הגיעו הצדדים בהסכם הכולל
title_en: Collective Agreement — Completion and Correction of the Agreements Reached by the Parties in the Comprehensive Agreement
summary_en: The large amending agreement to the Ofek Hadash comprehensive agreement of 25.12.2008: 94 sections that rewrite or add to roughly eighty-five sections of it and replace its annex tables. On pay it does three things. First, for an existing teacher converting to reform terms in school year 5772, 5773 or 5774, the salary used in the conversion formula is deemed increased by 3.5% (§ 88), applied by a re-conversion effective 1.3.2012 for those who converted in 5772 before signature. Second, a teacher who under the comprehensive agreement never converts gets a new 3.5% supplement on combined salary, 'Tosefet Shchika 2011', from the later of the reform's implementation at his institution or 1.3.2012 (§ 89), and in exchange all the collective-agreement provisions on erosion of teachers' pay against engineers' pay are abolished (§ 91). Third, it implements the further tranches of the 12.1.2011 framework cost (§ 92): from 1.1.2012 the reform salary tables are updated so the cumulative increase over the pre-1.1.2011 tables is 4% and Tosefet 2011 rises to 4%; the tranche due from January 2013 is deferred three months to April 2013 and cut by 0.5% to a top-up of 5.75%; and the tranche due from July 2013 is cut by 0.4% to a top-up of 6.35%. It also replaces the working-week tables from 1.9.2010 and the combined-salary tables from 1.3.2011, restates the mother-teacher relief as one frontal hour plus one stay hour a week instead of 2.5 stay hours from 1.9.2011, opens the 18-hour school-activity entitlement to principals and first deputies from 1.9.2010, adds a chapter paying principals of junior highs attached to six-year schools 95% of the principals' table, restarts the salary tables at seniority 1 rather than 0, sets a graded field-trip escort supplement, and lets overpayments arising from conversion errors be recovered in twelve equal instalments until 31.8.2014.

title_en: Supreme Follow-up Committee decision — the stay periods required for promotion to ranks 2 through 6 (and the 1,800-post quota for ranks 7–9)
summary_en: Acting under § 160 of the 25.12.2008 Ofek Hadash agreement, the Supreme Follow-up Committee replaces §§ 38(b), 38(f) and 38(i) with effect from 1.3.2015. Promotion from rank 1 to 2 and from 2 to 3 now requires two years and one month in the previous rank; promotion from 3 to 4, 4 to 5, 5 to 6, 6 to 7, 7 to 8 and 8 to 9 requires three years and one month. A teacher who meets the conditions for ranks 7–9 may not be held back longer than three years and one month (rank 7), four years and one month (rank 8) or five years and one month (rank 9), subject to a free quota. Notwithstanding § 38(g) the committee approves a one-off quota of 1,800 posts for promotion to ranks 7–9 across school years תשע"ד and תשע"ה, filled in three priority tiers effective 1.9.2014, 1.8.2015 (retirees leaving on 31.8.2015) and 1.9.2015 (highest תשע"ה evaluation results); teachers already sitting in ranks 7–9 at signature, and the vacancies then open for rank 9, are outside the quota. Registered as collective agreement no. 74/2015 on 21.6.2015.

title_en: Collective Agreement — applying part of the framework agreement's cost to teaching staff, and allocating a cost envelope for wage supplements and monetary benefits
summary_en: For 27.8.2013–31.12.2015 the agreement allocates a 3.5% cost envelope for wage supplements and monetary benefits, released in three tranches: 1% from 1.9.2016 and 1.5% from 1.3.2017, each distributed as a uniform shekel amount identical for every teacher at the same post fraction regardless of rank, and 1% from 1.1.2018 to be distributed as later agreed or, failing agreement, as a percentage supplement. The base for the envelope is the January–December 2015 monthly average of combined salary plus every supplement computed on it plus tosefet 94 and tosefet 87. It adds a one-off grant of NIS 1,000 under Wage Commissioner circular 2016-1-13. It replaces the combined-salary tables with new ones effective 1.9.2016 (appendices א'1–א'7, all seven present in this copy; the BA rank-1 seniority-1 cell is NIS 5,805.65 and the MA equivalent NIS 6,095.93), and creates a shekel 'wage-protection supplement 2016' Z = X − Y for any teacher whose new table salary is lower than the old, eroded by the amount of every subsequent pay rise. Finally, notwithstanding § 38(g) of the Ofek Hadash agreement, it approves a one-off promotion to ranks 7–9, backdated to 1.9.2015, for teachers who by 31.8.2015 had three years in the previous rank, the required professional-development hours and sufficient תשע"ב evaluation results. Registered as collective agreement no. 43/2016 on 15.6.2016.

title_en: Collective Agreement — applying the Ofek Hadash reform to teaching staff serving as SHELACH teachers (field, nation and society studies)
summary_en: Brings SHELACH teachers (field, nation and society studies) into Ofek Hadash on the junior-high model: a 100% post is a 36-hour week made up of 23 weekly frontal hours (which include trips, field activity and field days), 4 individual hours and 9 presence hours, worked over five days a week — or four days where the school already runs a five-day week and the teacher previously worked four, provided no day exceeds nine hours. Pay follows the current Ofek Hadash combined-salary tables, with placement under § 36, rank promotion under §§ 38 and 42, role supplements under §§ 39 and 41, and salary conversion under §§ 43–46 with the conversion coefficient Y taken from the junior-high model. Hourly value is the wage base divided by 4.33 weeks × 36 hours, with the pre-agreement base retained for substitution hours. Pension contributions follow § 151, and the determinative salary for budgetary pension is split into a pre-reform and a post-reform period. It also pays a one-off grant of NIS 10,000 for the period 1.9.2013–31.8.2015, pro-rated by weighted post fraction, which is not salary for any purpose and carries no fund contributions. Registered as collective agreement no. 100/2016 on 19.7.2016.

title_en: Collective Agreement — amendment of the September 2016 agreement: cost allocation, rank promotion and salary tables
summary_en: Rewrites the 30.9.2016 agreement and adds new supplements. It extends the agreement's term (and its claims-exhaustion and industrial-peace undertakings) from 30.6.2018 to 30.6.2019; inserts §§ 4(ג1) and 4(ג2) promoting to ranks 7, 8 or 9 teachers placed after conversion at ranks 6, 6.5, 7, 7.5, 8 or 8.5 who had never been promoted (from the day their conditions were met) and teachers at those ranks not promoted since 1.9.2013 who met the conditions by 31.12.2016 (from 1.4.2017), with arrears paid in the April 2017 payroll. It replaces the shekel supplement (tosefet sheklit) schedule: NIS 108.18 for every teacher from 1.9.2016 to 28.2.2017; from 1.3.2017 to 31.5.2019 NIS 340.17 at rank 1, 319.78 at 1.5, 299.39 at 2, 246.52 at 2.5 and 193.64 for everyone else; from 1.6.2019 NIS 648.48 / 628.09 / 607.70 / 554.83 / 501.96; from 1.9.2019 NIS 730.83 / 703.73 / 676.64 / 643.85 / 611.07 / 593.51 / 575.96 / 538.96 / 501.96 across ranks 1 to 4.5; and from 1.9.2020 NIS 1,074.37 / 1,011.48 / 948.59 / 872.47 / 796.36 / 755.61 / 714.86 / 628.96 / 543.33. It rewrites the 2016 wage-protection supplement so that X and Y both include role, doctorate and trailing-management supplements, fixes the comparison against the tables in force on 31.8.2016, and cancels the supplement outright once the teacher rises a rank or half-rank after 1.9.2016. It creates new role supplements: from 1.9.2017 a new § 39B paying 6% of combined salary to an integration and special-populations coordinator, to a learning-function assessor (MATAL) in a junior high and to a trips coordinator, and 2.4% per intern to a mentor teacher or mentor kindergarten teacher; and from 1.9.2019 a new § 39C paying 6% to a pedagogical (curriculum-planning) coordinator — each also payable at reform rates to non-reform teachers in the same roles. From 1.9.2019 it raises the counselling supplement in § 131 from 6% to 8% and from 9% to 12%. It abolishes § 7 of the September 2016 agreement and replaces its appendix ה' with a new coefficient table (X) driving the increase in the determinative pension salary, and the jubilee-grant base, for teachers who retired between 1.1.2013 and 31.8.2020. Registered as collective agreement no. 120/2017 on 15.6.2017.

From 1.9.2022 it replaces the combined-salary tables with appendices א1–א8 (a further table א9 replacing א8 from 1.9.2023) and pays 'Tosefet Ofek 2022', a rank-scaled shekel supplement pro-rated to post fraction and treated as salary for percentage supplements, hourly value, severance, pension and study-fund purposes — NIS 792.77 at rank 1 down to NIS 0.00 at rank 9 for BA teachers and NIS 832.44 down to NIS 0.00 for MA teachers, doubling from 1.9.2023 — both paid from the January 2023 payroll retroactive to 1.9.2022. title_he: הסכם קיבוצי מאושר — הפחתת שכר 2025-2026, כקבוע בחוק
title_en: Approved Collective Agreement — Wage Reduction 2025–2026, as Provided by Law
summary_en: This is the "approved collective agreement" (הסכם קיבוצי מאושר) required by the Law for the Participation of Public-Service Employees in Fiscal Stabilisation Measures during 2025 and 2026 (Temporary Provision), 5785-2025, for State-employed teaching staff on Ofek Hadash terms (instructors in supervision and headquarters posts and teacher-training colleges excluded). It cuts salary by 0.95% of the "determining base" for 1.5.2025-31.12.2025 and by 1.2% for 1.1.2026-31.12.2026, executed from the May 2025 salary paid in June 2025, and cuts the study-fund base by the same rates; pensions, severance and budgetary-pension computations are shielded, and the whole cut appears on one payslip line called "חוק הת. כלכלית אופק". It also claws back the 2025 clothing allowance (the CPI-linkage difference plus 91 NIS for a full post), withholds the September 2025 seniority-step increase through December 2025, moves the school-role supplement in § 22.1 of the 19.10.2022 agreement from school year תשפ"ו (1.9.2025) to תשפ"ז (1.9.2026), and freezes gmul shiluv and gmul pitzul for תשפ"ו and September-December 2026. Finally it defers 20 million NIS and a further 45 million NIS of fund transfers into 2026 and requires each teacher to work one extra frontal substitution hour in תשפ"ו, paid at 25% of hourly value.

summary_en: A temporary first stage of the reform for State-employed teaching staff to whom the 10.9.2007 reform agreement's pay and employment structure had not yet been applied (excluding full-time instructors, ulpan and adult-education teachers, supervisors, and teachers in reform schools who chose not to move to reform terms). From 1.1.2008 a teacher who performs one weekly individual teaching hour receives a 4.5% supplement computed on combined salary, the 1994 supplement and the 2001 supplement; from 1.1.2009 a second weekly individual hour adds a further 4%, making 8.5%. The rates assume a post of at least 75%, with smaller posts owing fewer individual hours (monthly rather than weekly), and the supplement is paid in proportion to the post fraction but not above 100%; it counts for percentage supplements computed on combined salary but not for hourly value. Principals instead work an extra hour organising and monitoring the individual hours, kindergarten teachers add ten minutes to the end of each school day, and payment stops after the June 2008 salary unless a comprehensive reform agreement is signed by then.

title_en: Collective Agreement — Wage Reduction by Deferring the Wage-Update Date
summary_en: A global-financial-crisis measure: instead of cutting rates, it postpones two scheduled increases for State-employed teaching staff (and for teachers of any other public employer that joins). In § 4(a)(3) of the 21.2.2008 agreement, "the December 2009 salary" becomes "the October 2011 salary" — deferring the top-up of the public-sector supplement to 5% by nearly two years — and in § 35(b)(1) of the 25.12.2008 Ofek Hadash comprehensive agreement, 1.12.2009 becomes 1.10.2011 for the salary-table update, with the § 47 dates adjusted to match. The pay not received is disregarded when computing end-of-employment payments and budgetary pensions, but is taken into account for provident-fund contributions. The agreement only enters into force once the legislation for partial payment of recreation pay in the public service in 2009 and 2010 is completed.

title_he: הסכם קיבוצי — קיצור הדחייה של מועד עדכון שכר
title_en: Collective Agreement — Shortening the Deferral of the Wage-Update Date
summary_en: Having agreed that teaching staff's share of the crisis measures was exhausted by the deferral carried out to 31.10.2010, the parties bring the two postponed updates forward by roughly eleven months. In § 4(a)(3) of the 21.2.2008 agreement as amended on 17.6.2009, "the October 2011 salary" becomes "the November 2010 salary", and in § 35(b)(1) of the 25.12.2008 Ofek Hadash comprehensive agreement as so amended, 1.10.2011 becomes 1.11.2010. The parties further agree that no change is needed to the § 47 dates because § 47 ("future computation and placement") applies only to the dates in §§ 4(a)(1) and 4(a)(2) of the 21.2.2008 agreement and not to § 4(a)(3), other economic consideration having been given instead and already being implemented. The agreement applies to State-employed teaching staff and to teachers of other public employers that join it.

title_en: Collective Agreement — Clothing Allowance for Teaching Staff
summary_en: From the clothing allowance paid in the July 2011 salary, every State-employed member of the teaching-staff grade becomes entitled to a level 4 clothing allowance irrespective of professional seniority, displacing the seniority-graded levels that applied before. The uplift is expressly only part of the bargain leading to a "completion agreement" amending and completing the 25.12.2008 Ofek Hadash agreement: if that completion agreement is not signed by 30.6.2012, the clothing allowance reverts to the earlier rules and any teacher with less than 25 years' professional seniority who was paid at level 4 must repay the difference between level 4 and level 3, which the State may set off against salary subject to the Wage Protection Law.

title_he: הסכם קיבוצי — זכויות הוריות – תוספת מעונות
title_en: Collective Agreement — Parental Rights: Childcare (Ma'onot) Allowance
summary_en: This applies § 11 of the 12.1.2011 general public-sector framework agreement to State-employed teaching staff. From 1.9.2011 the former "tosefet ma'onot" is replaced by a reimbursement of expenses for keeping a child under 5 in a nursery or other care: 300 NIS a month for one or the first child and 200 NIS a month for a second child, paid to a mother without receipts, for at most two children at a time; the amounts are for a 100% post, reduced in proportion for a smaller post and not increased above the full-post amount for a larger one. From January 2012 the amounts are uprated once a year in the January salary by the change in the consumer price index, the first update measured against the December 2010 index. The allowance is an expense reimbursement and not salary, is not paid for periods covered by maternity benefit or unpaid leave, and from the September 2011 salary supersedes every other arrangement for a child under 5. The agreement runs to 31.12.2012, with payments and differentials made from the October 2011 salary and at the latest the November 2011 salary.

title_he: חוזר תשסז/1 - עדכון פרטי בעלות
title_en: Circular 5767/1 — Updating the School Operator's ('Ba'alut') Contact Details
summary_en: Purely administrative: asks each school 'ba'alut' (the licensed body operating a non-state-run educational institution) to send the Ministry an updated contact — the responsible officer's name and title, the ba'alut's name, phone, and postal address — so that service-condition circulars for teaching staff reach the right person. title_he: חוזר תשסז/2 - היקפי משרת מנהלי בתי ספר על יסודיים
title_en: Circular 5767/2 — Employment Scope for Principals of Post-Primary Schools
summary_en: Raises, from 1.9.2006, the ceiling on employment scope for principals of large post-primary (secondary) schools from 150% to 175% of a position, but only for principals who already worked above 150% in the three years before the 5.12.2002 scope-of-position agreement and whose school has over 1,000 students, and only where the employer agrees to fund the excess. Requires the ba'alut to report qualifying principals annually.

title_he: חוזר תשסז/3 - קיזוז שכר מעובדי הוראה בשל עיצומים/שביתות במערכת החינוך בשנת הלימודים תשס"ז
title_en: Circular 5767/3 — Salary Deduction from Teaching Staff for Sanctions/Strikes in the Education System in the 5767 (2006-07) School Year
summary_en: Lists eight specific dates between 4.1.2007 and 11.3.2007 on which teachers' organisations held sanctions/strikes, and directs school operators to deduct pay from every teacher who took part, computed from each teacher's own fixed weekly teaching-hours schedule. The Ministry will recover the deducted amount from operators via the March 2007 'mat"m' transfer payments. Sets no new rate or formula; applies the ordinary no-work-no-pay rule to these named dates.

summary_en: Creates a new annual 'retention grant' (מענק התמדה), running for school years 5774-5777, for veteran teachers (25 years' seniority in official/upper-secondary schools, or 30 years elsewhere) who teach a listed required subject (e.g. maths, physics, chemistry, computer science, English) and have at least 10 years' service in the formal education system. title_en: Owners' Circular 5780/1 – Employment of Owner-Employed Teaching Staff at Recognised-Not-Official Special-Education Schools under the New Horizon Reform, 5780 School Year
summary_en: Following a Supreme Court commitment (HCJ 148/18, WIZO v. Ministry of Education), extends the New Horizon reform's terms to teaching staff at recognised-not-official special-education schools from the 5780 school year, equalising their teaching resources with official special-education schools. Sets joining-eligibility conditions, a 36-hour workweek structure (elementary: 26 frontal + 5 individual + 5 standby hours; secondary: 23 frontal + 4 individual + 9 standby hours), promotion tables giving 7.5% (teachers) or 8.75% (principals/deputies) per grade step on defined seniority/professional-development thresholds, a schedule of role stipends (deputy principal 13%, class teacher 10-11.5%, subject coordinator 6-8%, etc.), advance-payment percentages pending formal grade determination (14-27% by post/role), and worked wage-conversion formulas for reclassifying existing staff into the New Horizon salary tables.

advance payment pending formal grade determination: 17%/14% (elementary teachers/interns), 27%/22% (secondary teachers/interns), 20%/15% (deputy principals/principals)

title_he: חוזר לבעלויות תשפ"א/1
title_en: Circular to Owners, Tashpa/1 (2020–2021 school year)
summary_en: Extends the Ofek Hadash (New Horizon) reform's pay structure and work-week rules to teaching staff at recognized-but-unofficial special-education schools for the 2020-21 school year, implementing a State undertaking made in HCJ 148/18 (WIZO v. Ministry of Education) to equalize teaching resources with official special-education schools. Fixes the weekly work-hour split (frontal/individual/waiting hours) by education stage, role-holder grant percentages (e.g. 13% second deputy principal, 10%/11.5% homeroom teacher, 6-10% subject/social/pedagogic coordinators, 8%/12% counseling grant), rank-promotion tables (7.5% per rank for teachers, 8.75% for principals/deputies, gated by months of service and professional-development hours), and interim 'Ofek Hadash advance' percentages (14-27%) paid pending each teacher's rank determination, plus worked salary-conversion formulas for moving existing staff onto the new tables.

It also ends the outstanding advance-salary deduction that Circular 5784/8 had begun, rolling any remaining balance into the one-time bonus payment.

title_en: Law for Achieving the Budget Targets and Implementing Economic Policy for Budget Year 2025 (Legislative Amendments), 5785-2025 — Chapter 9: Law on the Participation of Employees and Office-Holders in the Public Service in Measures to Stabilise the State's Fiscal Position during 2025 and 2026 (Hora'at Sha'a — Temporary Order), 5785-2025
summary_en: A temporary order that cuts public-sector pay across the board for two defined windows: 3.307% of the "determining base" (ha-basis ha-kove'a) during the first determining period, 1 April 2025 to 31 December 2025, and 1.2% during the second determining period, 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2026. Teachers are squarely inside it: "employer" expressly includes an education institution whose government funding was at least 40% of its 2024 budget, and "education employee" covers anyone employed at an education institution whose main occupation is teaching, education or educational supervision. Where an approved collective agreement (signed by 31 March 2025 and approved by the Minister of Finance or the Wage Commissioner) sets its own reduction, that agreement governs instead, and a cut already taken in the preliminary period of 1 December 2024 to 31 March 2025 may be credited against it. The base excludes recreation pay (dmei havra'a), clothing allowance, expense reimbursements, tax gross-up and any payment not computed monthly/weekly/daily; the same percentage is applied to the base for study-fund (keren hishtalmut) contributions, but the cut is disregarded for pension-fund contributions, the pensionable determining salary, budgetary pension, severance and National Insurance benefits. The withheld money is never repaid (§9) and each employer must compute the saving and remit it to the State Treasury.
amends: Overrides, for the duration of the temporary order, any "הסכם" fixing the salary — collective agreement, extension order (צו הרחבה), collective arrangement including a unilateral arrangement, administrative directive (הוראת מינהל), or personal/special employment contract under s.40 of the Civil Service (Appointments) Law 5719-1959

חוק הקפאת שכר נושאי משרה ברשויות השלטון וברשויות מקומיות בשנת 2025, התשפ"ה-2024 ("the office-holders freeze law") — §5 carves out employees whose salary is set by reference to an office-holder's salary: neither the freeze nor this chapter's reduction applies to them indirectly
Government Decision no. 742 of 20 Tammuz 5783 (9 July 2023) — governs the reduction for soldiers in place of §§2-3
Government Decisions no. 397 of 7 Shevat 5739 (4 February 1979) and no. 743 of 20 Tammuz 5783 (9 July 2023) — govern the reduction for police officers and prison officers

חוק שירות המדינה (גמלאות) [נוסח משולב], התש"ל-1970 ss.50, 57 and חוק שירות הקבע בצה"ל (גמלאות) [נוסח משולב], התשמ"ה-1985 — amended by the containing Act (limitation period for a survivor's pension claim extended from two years to four)

The containing Act (outside Chapter 9) also amends the Fines Collection Centre Law 5755-1995, the Execution Law 5727-1967, the Government Companies Law 5735-1975, the Water and Sewage Corporations Law 5761-2001, the Income Tax Ordinance, the VAT Law 5736-1975, the Land Taxation Law 5723-1963 and the National Insurance Law 5755-1995

title_he: תקנון שירות עובדי הוראה
title_en: Takanon Sherut Ovdei Hora'a (Teaching Staff Service Regulations)
summary_en: The Ministry of Education's consolidated service regulations for teaching staff — the master rulebook that defines what a teacher's pay is made of and who is entitled to each part. §1.1 enumerates the components: combined salary (shakar meshulav) by seniority, rank and post fraction from the salary table (§1.29), plus the 3% 2001 supplement from 1.1.2001, the 2008 supplement rising 1.5% → 3% → 5%, and the 2011 supplement rising 2.25% → a uniform 4%. It then fixes the individual supplements and grants: the jubilee grant (ma'anak yovel) at 60% of the pension/severance determining salary from 30 years' cumulative seniority (25 for state-service teachers from 1.6.2008, §1.46); second- and third-degree supplements of 5% and 10% of combined salary (§1.47); the special-education supplement at 14% of combined salary in a wholly special-education setting and 9% in an integrative one (§4.6); the mother-teacher supplement for a teacher with a child under 14 employed at 79% of a post or more (§1.13); and clothing allowance, recreation pay, travel, split-teaching gmul, incentives and age-hours across §§1.6-1.24. Chapters 2 through 8 attach role-specific gmulim to kindergarten teachers, primary, junior-high and post-primary teachers, special-education staff, principals and deputies, instructors and supervisors.
amends: §1.1(c) note — defers implementation of the 2008 supplement to October 2011 for teaching staff employed in the state service in official education (kindergartens, primary schools, junior highs, special-education schools), for staff in recognised-unofficial kindergartens, primary schools (including the education networks) and junior highs, for staff in teacher-training colleges, and for staff in government post-primary schools
numbers: 3% supplement on the combined salary from 1.1.2001, paid on a separate payslip line but counting as salary for contributions and for computing gmulim (§1.1(b))
2008 supplement: 1.5% from 1.2.2008, completed to 3% from 1.1.2009 and to 5% from 1.1.2010 (§1.1(c))
2011 supplement: 2.25% from 1.1.2011 computed on combined salary + 2001 supplement + 2008 supplement, rising to a uniform 4% from 1.1.2012 (§1.1(d))
jubilee grant: 60% of the determining salary for pension and severance, excluding one-off annual payments such as clothing and recreation (§1.46)

jubilee grant seniority threshold: 30 years' cumulative teaching seniority including military service; 25 years for teaching staff employed in the state service and graded on the teaching scale, effective 1.6.2008 (§1.46)
a year of unpaid leave for which the teacher paid 18.5% of salary to purchase rights counts toward jubilee-grant seniority (§1.46 clarification (a))
second-degree supplement 5% of combined salary; doctorate supplement 10% of combined salary (§1.47)

special-education supplement: 14% of combined salary for a qualified special-education teacher in a special-education kindergarten, school, institution, MAPTAN or special-education class in a regular school; 9% of combined salary in other frameworks recognised within regular education as an integration teacher (§4.6)
mother-teacher: applies to a teacher who is mother to a child up to age 14 and works at least a 79% post (§1.13)
clothing allowance level 1 covers 1-25 years' teaching seniority, with the level set by seniority (§1.6)

lesson length: of the first four lessons, 2 of 50 minutes and 2 of 45 minutes; a class taking 4 unjoined lessons must be present at school at least 240 minutes, 230 minutes where joined lessons are given, and 170 minutes for a special-school class taking only 3 lessons (§1.22)
caveats: The plain-text copy flattens every table. The clothing-allowance amounts per seniority level (§1.6), the salary tables behind §1.29, and the role-gmul percentage tables in chapters 2-8 are therefore not readable from the .txt — only their headings and the surrounding prose survive. The HTML must be consulted for those figures.

The mirror is a snapshot dated 2026-06-01, but the takanon carries no single instrument date. Individual sections carry their own 'this section was updated on' stamps ranging from 26.5.2002 to 24.6.2012 (24 such stamps), so parts of the text predate the Ofek Hadash reform and are stale relative to it.

Chapters 9 (teaching staff teaching practical engineers and technicians), 10 (working-youth schools), 11 (teacher-training institutions) and 14 (adult education) appear only as navigation entries in this extraction; no body text for them is present.

Several section numbers cited in the table of contents have no corresponding page in the extraction, among them 1.2-1.5, 1.16, 1.20, 3.2, 3.10-3.11, 3.17, 4.3, 4.5, 4.7-4.9, 5.2-5.3, 5.7-5.10, 6.2, 6.4, 6.7-6.8, 6.12, 6.14-6.15 and 6.19.
Site navigation menus and the full chapter index are interleaved with body text throughout the extraction, so a bare grep for a section number will often hit the menu rather than the section.
The extraction preserves a few Hebrew typos from the source, e.g. 'בשיעורים כדלeמן' for 'כדלקמן' in §4.6.

title_he: תחום תנאי שירות עובדי הוראה
title_en: Teaching Staff Terms of Service Division
summary_en: The landing page of the Ministry of Education's Teaching Staff Terms of Service Division, within the Senior Division for Teaching Manpower. It states what the division does rather than setting any entitlement: it administers the employment terms of roughly 230,000 teaching staff — kindergarten teachers, teachers and principals in official and recognised-unofficial education, across all age stages and sectors — through three lines of work, namely publishing and updating the Takanon Sherut Ovdei Hora'a, publishing new salary tables and new service terms in circulars to the employing bodies (be'aluyot), and giving information and guidance to enquirers inside and outside the Ministry. It gives the division's contact details: 15 Kanfei Nesharim Street, Jerusalem, telephone 073-3935138, fax 073-3935190.
numbers: approximately 230,000 teaching staff whose employment terms the division administers
address 15 Kanfei Nesharim Street, Jerusalem; telephone 073-3935138; fax 073-3935190
caveats: The page is a two-paragraph departmental description with no date and no normative content; it is the index for the takanon and salary-table pages beneath it rather than an instrument in its own right.
The akn identifier's 2026-06-01 is the mirror snapshot date, not a date the page carries.

title_he: שאלות ותשובות
title_en: Questions and Answers (Teaching Staff Terms of Service portal)
summary_en: The Terms of Service Division's official answers to recurring entitlement questions, organised by pay component: split-teaching gmul, travel expenses, management seniority, summer and festival leave, sick leave, trip escorting, mother-teacher supplement, role appointments and gmulim, jubilee grant, clothing allowance, study funds, age hours and the special-education supplement. It settles eligibility conditions that the takanon leaves open — that only a homeroom class counts toward the class tally for split-teaching gmul, that matriculation-preparation hours do not count toward the "within one post" limit even though they otherwise rank as teaching hours, and that a teacher must have worked before and after a festival to be paid for it while paid sick days and maternity leave count as work. It states the computation formulas outright: the counsellor's gmul is the full seniority-based gmul multiplied by actual counselling hours and divided by 12, on a base of combined salary + the 3% 2001 supplement + the 1994 teaching-agreement supplement; unused sick days below 36% utilisation redeem at 8 days' pay per 30 unused days, valued at 1/25 of the monthly salary at 100% post; and the special-education supplement is 5.5% (unqualified, integrative), 9% (unqualified, wholly special education), 8.5% (qualified, integrative) or 14% (qualified, wholly special education). It also fixes the mother-teacher supplement at 10% of the salary for a 100% post, payable automatically at a 79% post with one employer and split pro rata between employers where the teacher reaches 79%-140% across two.
numbers: split-teaching gmul requires at least 6 classes taught within the limits of one post, or 4 classes for mother tongue or a foreign language

counsellor's gmul = (full gmul by counselling seniority × actual weekly counselling hours) ÷ 12, on a base of combined salary + 3% (2001 agreement supplement) + the 1994 teaching-agreement supplement; the worked example uses a combined salary of 3,308 NIS at a 100% post, 99 NIS for the 3% supplement and 124 NIS for the 1994 supplement, total 3,531 NIS, a 7% gmul rate at 3 years' counselling seniority giving 247 NIS, and 6 weekly counselling hours giving 247 × 6 ÷ 12 = 123.5 NIS

sick-day redemption: below 36% lifetime utilisation, 8 days' pay for every 30 unused days; the worked example is 594 days accrued and 55 used = 9.26% utilisation, 539 unused days, 539 × 8 ÷ 30 = 143.7 rounded to 144 days' pay, each day valued at 1/25 of the monthly salary at a 100% post

special-education supplement: 5.5% for a teacher not qualified in special education teaching in an integrative framework, 9% for an unqualified teacher in a wholly special-education framework, 8.5% for a qualified teacher in an integrative framework, 14% for a qualified teacher in a wholly special-education framework

mother-teacher supplement: 10% of the salary for a 100% post, paid automatically where the teacher works at least a 79% post with one employer; where she works under 79% at one employer but reaches 79%-140% across two, each employer pays the 10% pro rata to its share (worked example: 50% + 40% = 90%, so employer A pays 10% × 50/90 and employer B pays 10% × 40/90)
a teacher at a 79%-or-more post with one employer receives the 10% from that employer alone and gets nothing from a second employer where she works under 80%
jubilee grant is due in the year in which payslip seniority in teaching in Israel plus IDF seniority reaches 30
age hours: a teacher reaching the qualifying age by 31 December is entitled to age hours from the start of that school year; reaching it from 1 January defers entitlement to the following school year
a principal or deputy principal reaching age 50 gets full age hours if teaching two-thirds of a full post — 16 weekly hours where the post base is 24, or 20 where the base is 30
post-base example: a teacher moving from a 24-hour to a 22-hour post base stays tenured at 100% of a post, not at a fixed number of hours

travel: a teacher attending school twice a week or less is reimbursed actual travel costs; more than two days a week, the price of a free monthly pass pro rata to days worked; a teacher driving in from outside the city is reimbursed at the public-transport tariff for the real distance

summer-holiday pay is proportional to post fraction and to the period worked during the school year — half a school year worked yields half the summer holiday paid; paid sick leave and maternity leave count as work for this purpose
sick-leave pay in a subsequent school year is recalculated to 100% of a post and without the homeroom gmul where the teacher has no tenure on the role or on the post fraction above 100%
caveats: The page carries no date of its own; the akn identifier's 2026-06-01 is the mirror snapshot date. Several answers are anchored to school years 5762-5763 (2001/02-2002/03) and to a worked example using a combined salary of 3,308 NIS, so the illustrative amounts are long out of date even though the formulas they demonstrate are the point.

Answers cross-refer to takanon sections (1.25.3.2 for sick-day redemption, 1.26.1.2 for the training gmul) without reproducing them; the rules are only fully stated when read together with takanon/takanon-sherut-ovdei-horaa.html.

The fraction bars in the worked examples do not survive text extraction: numerator and denominator appear on separate lines (e.g. '55 = 9.26%' followed by '594'), so each computation had to be reconstructed from context.
Raw Akoma Ntoso element ids ('hc_1__para_la__subpara_la__cls_la') are left dangling at the end of the extracted text.

title_he: חוזרים ונהלים לבעלויות
title_en: Circulars and Procedures for Owners (be'aluyot — the bodies that own and operate educational institutions and employ their teaching staff)
summary_en: This is the Ministry of Education's chronological index of its circulars to owners (חוזרים לבעלויות) and of its procedures, running year by year from תשס"א (2000-01) through תשפ"ז (2026-27), with 53 named annexes. It is the channel by which the Commissioner for Teaching Staff Service Conditions transmits pay instructions to the bodies that employ teaching staff: the recurring annual series covers clothing allowance (קצובת ביגוד), recreation pay and the jubilee grant (דמי הבראה ומענק יובל), the annual update of the tosefet shiklit 2016 shekel supplement and, in the upper division, of תוספת 87 for principals crossing to the Oz LeTmura reform, the school-achievement bonus, and salary deductions for strikes and school closures. It also indexes the circulars that apply particular instruments — the 19.10.2022 wage agreement for the period 1.1.2020 to 31.12.2026 (circulars תשפ"ג/4 and תשפ"ג/5), the general collective agreement of 12.9.2023 (תשפ"ד/4), the 23.09.2024 agreement with the upper-secondary teachers' organisation (תשפ"ה/5), the teacher-training-colleges agreement of 19.08.2024 (תשפ"ה/4), and the application to teaching staff of the 2025 fiscal-stabilisation temporary-provision law for 2025 and 2026 (תשפ"ה/9) — together with the annual Ofek Hadash employment circulars for recognised-but-unofficial special-education schools and kindergartens and their joining undertakings, rank-setting and salary-conversion booklets, and the employment-approval and over-full-post procedures. The page itself sets no rate: it names each circular and its annexes, and the circulars' own texts lie outside it.

Several entries in the mirrored text are truncated mid-date: the תשפ"ה/5 annex titles read 'להסכם שנחתם ב' with no date, and one reads '23.9.2)' for 23.9.2024.
One annex title carries a typo in the source: 'בדרגת בלתי מוסך' for 'בדרגת בלתי מוסמך'.
The Akoma Ntoso date 2016-09-01 is a corpus-assigned date; the page carries no date of its own and lists circulars through תשפ"ז (2026-27).

title_he: טבלת שכר
title_en: Salary Table
summary_en: This is the salary-scale page of the takanon: it carries a précis of 'the composition of the salary for teaching staff', stated as updated to June 2015 and compiled in coordination with the Wage and Labour Agreements Division of the Ministry of Finance, for teaching staff in pre-primary and primary institutions outside the Ofek Hadash reform, and it indexes the binding salary tables by reform status, rank class and effective date. The pre-reform combined-salary tables are listed for academics and certified staff (אקדמאים ומוסמכים), uncertified staff (בלתי מוסמכים) and the instructor rank (דרגת מדריך), each in four versions: valid from 1/1/2008, from 1/1/2007, from 1/6/2006, and up to 31/5/2006. For the upper division it indexes the tables under the wage agreement of 14.3.2018 (annexes א to ד); for Ofek Hadash it indexes nineteen annexes under the agreement of 19/10/2022 — the BA and MA salary tables (א1, א2), the tosefet Ofek 2022 supplement tables (ב1+ג1, ב2+ג, ב3+ג3, ב4+ג4, ב5+ג5, ב6+ג6, ב7+ג7), the conversion tables for serving teachers at BA, MA, senior (בכיר), certified (מוסמך) and uncertified rank (א3 to א7), and deputies and principals (א8, א9) — plus deputy-principal tables from 1/9/2022 and from 1/9/2023 for certified, senior, intern (מתמחה) and uncertified deputies, and the Ofek Hadash tables updated to 1/9/2016. It states that where it conflicts with the existing directives and collective agreements, those govern.
caveats: The page holds no figures: the mirrored HTML contains no table and no row, only the nineteen annex titles as dead in-page anchors, so the scales themselves are not in this corpus.
Several annex entries lose their effective date in the mirror, rendering as 'נספח א - החל מ' with nothing after 'from'.

The salary-composition précis flags itself as 'updated to June 2015', as concise, and as published 'for convenience, for reasons of efficiency only, without derogating from or replacing the existing directives and the full binding agreements'; where it conflicts with those, they determine.
kind_note: this register calls it salaryTable; the corpus's own Akoma Ntoso identifier says takanon

title_he: תקנון שירות עובדי הוראה
title_en: Service Regulations for Teaching Staff (takanon sherut ovdei hora'a)
summary_en: This is the front page of the takanon — the Ministry of Education's consolidated statement of the service and salary conditions of teaching staff, prepared by the Bureau of the Commissioner for Teaching Staff Service Conditions, in fourteen chapters: a general chapter applying to all teaching staff (salary, supplements, allowances and gemulim of every kind, resignation and dismissal of teachers, and the way rank and seniority are set), and further chapters by education stage and role (kindergarten teachers, primary-school teachers, teaching staff in management, instruction and inspection roles) covering the gemulim particular to each role and the manner of appointment and definition of duties. It fixes one rule of computation for the whole takanon: wherever the text says a supplement is 'X% of the combined salary' (שכר משולב), the base is every component that forms the calculation base for gemulim, except where the text says expressly that combined salary alone is meant. It subordinates itself to every other source: where the takanon does not match the collective agreements, the provisions of statute, director-general circulars, Ministry procedures or more recent circulars to owners, those prevail, and the binding text, application and scope of its provisions are those of the sources it cites.
caveats: The page flags that the takanon is itself in the process of being updated, and that wherever it conflicts with collective agreements, statute, director-general circulars, Ministry procedures or more recent circulars to owners, those override the takanon.
It flags that the sums printed in the takanon are deliberately not kept current, 'because of the frequency of the changes'; current amounts must be obtained from the Bureau.
The Akoma Ntoso date 2026-06-01 is the date of the mirror snapshot; the page carries no date of its own.

title_he: היערכות לפתיחת שנה
title_en: Preparing for the Opening of the School Year
summary_en: This is the takanon's hub for the procedures that must be followed before each school year opens, indexed year by year from תשע"ו (2015-16) to תשפ"ז (2026-27). For each year it lists the employment-approval procedure (נוהל אישור העסקה), the procedure for approving employment above a full post in official education and the corresponding procedure in recognised-but-unofficial education, and the procedure for intake and placement of candidates for teaching posts; for several years it also lists the kindergarten-teacher placement procedure, the procedure for employing a teaching-staff member above 100% of a post under the pre-reform working week or under the Oz LeTmura and Ofek Hadash agreements, the unpaid-leave (חל"ת) procedure, and the online procedures for opening a teaching-staff file, for principals and for districts. It records that the kindergarten placement procedure governs kindergarten teachers who are State employees, whose salary is paid by the State; that the Mishkit placement system has been adapted to the Ofek Hadash agreements and to the placement and tenure procedure for תשע"ה and תשע"ו; and that the procedure carries a table of the kindergarten working week, including for יוח"א kindergartens. It sets no rate and administers no payment directly: it governs approval, intake and placement, and the timetables those must meet.
numbers: 100% of a post (משרה) — the threshold above which employing a teaching-staff member requires the over-full-post approval procedure, under the pre-reform working-week structure or under the Oz LeTmura and Ofek Hadash agreements
caveats: The page flags its own drafting convention: wherever it writes גננת or גננות in the feminine, male kindergarten teachers are equally intended.
The page is an index of procedure titles; the procedures' own texts are not part of it and are not in this corpus.
The Akoma Ntoso date 2026-06-01 is the date of the mirror snapshot; the page carries no date of its own and indexes years through תשפ"ז (2026-27).
